beliefs: For strings of length 1, the single character is lowercased and '10' is prepended [E2, E4, E8]
For strings of length >=2, the first character is titlecased (str.title(), which may expand to multiple chars like 'ß'->'Ss', 'ﬁ'->'Fi', 'ǆ'->'ǅ') [E1, E2, E4, E9, E11]
All characters after the first are lowercased [E1, E2, E3]
The '10' is inserted at index floor(len/2) computed on the ORIGINAL string length, before any case transformation [E2, E4, E5, E6, E7, E9, E12, E13]
The rest-of-string lowercasing happens BEFORE insertion, so the index refers to the lowercased-rest string but the length used is the original length [E13]
Order of operations: lowercase rest, insert '10' at floor(original_len/2), then titlecase the first character (which may grow the string) [E9, E13]
For 'ßabc' -> 'Ssa10bc': '10' goes at index 2 (floor(4/2)), then 'ß'->'Ss' expands [E9]
For 'Aİxy' -> 'Ai̇10xy': rest 'İxy' lowercases to 'i̇xy' (length 4), '10' inserted at floor(4/2)=2 of original length 4, giving 'Ai̇10xy' [E13]
For 'AİBC' -> 'Ai̇10bc': rest 'İBC' lowercases to 'i̇bc' (length 4), '10' at index floor(4/2)=2, giving 'Ai̇10bc' [E13]
For 'ǆabc' -> 'ǅa10bc': titlecase of 'ǆ' is 'ǅ' (not upper 'Ǆ') [E9, E11]
For 'ﬁabc' -> 'Fia10bc' and 'ﬀab' -> 'Ff10ab': titlecase expands ligatures [E9, E11]
notes: E13 shows the insertion index uses the ORIGINAL string length (not the post-lowercase length), and the rest is lowercased before insertion. Fixed predict() to compute idx from len(s) and lowercase the rest before inserting.
